content.text: alright lets discuss the deliverable of this branch.

I’d make this branch deliver **one complete voice interaction with a blueprint**: the user speaks a question, sees the transcription, and hears the answer while the tool displays its evidence and highlights.

The demo flow would be:

1. Upload a plan or IFC using the existing interface.
2. Press a microphone button and ask a question.
3. Google transcribes speech live into the question field.
4. Submit the transcript through the existing Blueprint question pipeline.
5. Show the answer and citations, then read the answer aloud using ElevenLabs.
6. Allow the user to stop playback and ask another question.

For the first version, I suggest **push-to-talk with an editable transcript and explicit submission**. That’s our design choice to make question boundaries predictable and avoid submitting misheard dimensions or room names. It adds a click and won’t demonstrate fully hands-free conversation; automatic submission and interruption can follow if that matters for the demo.

The branch would deliver:

- Microphone controls, live transcript, and clear listening/processing/speaking states.
- Server-side Google transcription and ElevenLabs speech adapters, with credentials kept out of the browser.
- Integration with the existing answer pipeline, preserving evidence requirements and insufficient/unclear responses.
- Text fallback when either voice service fails.
- Deterministic adapter tests, setup instructions, and a live end-to-end verification when credentials are available.

One choice to settle first: by **Google live transcription**, do you mean **Google Cloud Speech-to-Text streaming**, or **Gemini Live API transcription**? I’d default to Speech-to-Text for this flow because we already have a separate system responsible for answering blueprint questions.

can you adjust what transcribe understands, e.g. some room names are pretty hard to pronounce or are unlikely to be understood wihtout the transcription model knowing that its valid, so is there basically a straight forward path to increase the words the transcription model understands

I’ll check how Google’s streaming transcription supports custom room names, and whether Gemini Live offers the same kind of vocabulary hints.


**Yes—there’s a straightforward path: supply the transcription model with a vocabulary of names from the current building.** No model training is needed.

Google supports this in both options:

- **Gemini Live transcription:** accepts a `custom_vocabulary` list containing room names, unusual words, and technical terms. [Google’s documentation](https://aistudio.google.com/docs/live-api/live-transcribe#custom-vocabulary-biasing)
- **Cloud Speech-to-Text:** supports phrase hints and custom classes, plus adjustable “boost” values to make particular terms more likely. Availability depends on the model and language. [Google’s adaptation guide](https://docs.cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/adaptation-model)

For Blueprint, I’d propose this flow:

1. Extract room names from the IFC properties or labels read from the drawing.
2. Include those names when starting the transcription session.
3. Allow user-defined aliases—for example, “plant room” referring to the room labelled “Talotekniikka.”
4. Keep the transcript editable when a name is still misunderstood.

Vocabulary hints help the recognizer choose an unusual name when the audio sounds like it. **Aliases are a separate application feature:** they let someone use an easier name and still refer to the correct room.

This improves recognition without guaranteeing it; excessive bias can also produce a room name that wasn’t spoken. We should compare the same recordings with and without hints, including questions that don’t mention any listed room. [Google’s boost guidance](https://docs.cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/adaptation-model#boost_basics)

I’d include **vocabulary specific to the uploaded building** in this branch’s deliverable. The documented Gemini Live support also means this requirement doesn’t force us to use Cloud Speech-to-Text.

content.text:
Proposed minimal implementation plan, based on current source and reviewed provider documentation:

1. Root copies current uncommitted Blueprint source into the dedicated worktree, preserving the original workspace. Root owns `app/main.py`, configuration/dependencies, `.env.example`, and documentation.
2. Backend owns new `app/voice*.py` and `tests/test_voice*.py`; frontend owns `app/static/app.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css`, new microphone/voice JS files, and `tests/test_voice_browser.py`. Independent reviewer remains read-only.
3. Begin dependent implementation after reviewer accepts the contract below.

**Contract**

- `GET /api/voice/config` returns readiness booleans, transcription model, and configured language hints. Readiness reports configuration only, never verified service access. Voice remains available independently of the QA provider setting.
- `GET /api/documents/{document_id}/voice-vocabulary` returns:
  ```json
  {
    "terms": ["Talotekniikka"],
    "rooms": [{"id": "...", "name": "Talotekniikka", "floor_label": "..."}],
    "warnings": []
  }
  ```
  Extract names from every `scene.elements` room, including geometry-less rooms, and available floor labels; normalize whitespace and deduplicate case-insensitively. No measurements/properties/assumptions go into recognition context. Generated names remain fallible hints, never factual QA evidence.

  Current `Document` retains a scene, not the extracted `BuildingDescription`. Therefore drawings gain automatic room hints after model generation; before that, accept manually supplied vocabulary and explain this limitation. Native IFC names are available immediately. Do not add an OCR/model call solely for vocabulary.

- WebSocket `/api/voice/transcribe`:
  - Initial client message: `{"type":"start","document_id":"...","custom_vocabulary":["..."]}`.
  - Server validates document and combines its current building vocabulary with manual terms and aliases.
  - Server emits `{"type":"ready"}` only after Google session opens.
  - Browser sends binary signed little-endian PCM16, mono, 16 kHz. An AudioWorklet must resample the actual browser sample rate rather than assuming 16 kHz.
  - Server emits `{"type":"transcript","text":"...","final":false|true}`. Finals append; interim text replaces the current interim hypothesis.
  - Client `{"type":"stop"}` ends input, flushes final recognition, then receives `{"type":"done"}`.
  - Client `{"type":"cancel"}` or disconnect immediately cancels downstream tasks and closes the provider session.
  - Safe `{"type":"error","message":"..."}` reports operational failures; never expose provider bodies, credentials, audio, vocabulary, or raw exceptions.

  Use `gemini-3.5-transcribe-live`, `response_modalities=["TEXT"]`, `input_audio_transcription.custom_vocabulary`, and current SDK streaming fields. Provider maximum is 1,000 vocabulary phrases: validate and report excess explicitly, never silently truncate. Root should explain this external limit before implementation. No additional arbitrary phrase, recording-duration, or room limits.

- `POST /api/voice/speech` accepts `{"document_id":"...","text":"..."}` and returns `audio/mpeg`; missing document remains 404, missing credentials 503, provider failures 502. Use ElevenLabs HTTP API via existing `httpx`, fixed server-configured voice/model, and MP3. Reuse the existing 6,000-character draft-answer bound. Browser sends the displayed `result.answer` verbatim, including insufficient/unclear answers; no answer rewrite or second LLM call.

  For this slice, fetching a complete MP3 blob before playback is acceptable and simpler to verify. Document the resulting startup latency. Stop must abort pending fetch, pause playback, revoke its object URL, and invalidate delayed results. Server should cancel upstream work on disconnect where feasible; do not promise that cancellation reverses already billed generation.

**User interaction and aliases**

- Click microphone to start; click Stop to finalize; edit transcript; click existing Ask button. No automatic question submission.
- Show connecting/listening/finalizing/synthesizing/speaking/error states separately from QA errors.
- Provide “Read answers aloud” preference and explicit Read/Stop controls. Preserve text and citations when TTS fails or browser autoplay is blocked.
- Add per-document custom terms and aliases. Alias maps a user-entered easy phrase to a selected room ID; use floor-qualified display labels for duplicated room names. Keep aliases in browser memory for this slice.
- Include aliases and target names in speech hints. Apply alias normalization visibly before Ask; retain original recognized text in a preview, with the editable submitted question showing any substitution. Use exact, case-insensitive Unicode word boundaries, longest-match-first, no fuzzy room selection and no recursive replacements. Ambiguous alias definitions require correction.
- Speech and recording must not run concurrently. Starting either stops the other.
- New upload, new question, cancellation, navigation, or failed connection must stop microphone tracks, disconnect the worklet, close the AudioContext/socket, and invalidate late callbacks. Use a voice generation token alongside existing `state.requestVersion`.

**Acceptance and verification**

- Fake live provider sees native/derived room names, floors, custom terms, aliases, Unicode names, and geometry-less rooms correctly; vocabulary never enters answer evidence.
- Missing scene still permits manual hints and ordinary transcription; generated IFC reopening restores name hints.
- Provider wire tests confirm supported configuration fields, PCM framing, interim/final semantics, stop flushing, cancellation, and safe error mapping.
- Alias tests cover duplicate room names/floors, Unicode boundaries, overlap/longest match, unknown targets, and no unintended substring replacement.
- Real browser tests use injected speech/QA providers and fake microphone audio: visible partial → final → editable question → existing QA answer/citation/highlight flow; insufficient/unclear speech preserves meaning.
- Browser tests verify permission denial, missing credentials, failed services, stopping while connecting/finalizing/synthesizing, upload replacement, late events, text fallback, and microphone cleanup. Include narrow-screen layout.
- Existing backend/browser suite passes. Independent implementation review clears blocking findings.
- Root performs live transcription and ElevenLabs smoke checks only when credentials are available, and records separate unverified integrations honestly. A/B recordings with and without vocabulary are needed before claiming recognition improvement.

Existing `google-genai==3.3.0`, `httpx`, and `websockets==17.4` cover implementation; root should make `websockets` an explicit dependency only if used directly or required by uvicorn’s server transport.

Defer continuous hands-free conversation, automatic submission, speech-driven model commands, voice cloning, persistence, and fuzzy entity resolution. These exclusions preserve the agreed explicit-submit flow rather than impose new input restrictions.

Plan revision accepted by independent reviewer; no remaining planning blockers.

- Google reception spans multiple VAD turns. Stop waits for terminal completion with a configurable 15-second deadline; timeout preserves finalized text and reports incomplete transcription.
- Test a pause-completion already in flight at Stop. Local event timing alone must not be presented as guaranteed finality.
- Native room floors come from `Storey.Name`; aliases expand visibly to floor-qualified names. Duplicate canonical targets are rejected.
- Speech accepts up to 6,000 characters with explicit text fallback, never truncation.
- Backend owns new voice modules/config/tests; root owns main integration, environment, dependencies, and documentation; frontend owns UI and browser checks.

Revised spoken-answer plan accepted by independent reviewer; no planning blockers.

- Compute `spoken_answer` and `spoken_answer_with_details` after validated answers and calculations.
- Preserve written answer, evidence, and highlights unchanged.
- Remove narrowly recognized technical metadata; retain measurements, ordinary window labels, and every uncertainty qualifier.
- Always append labelled missing-information and next-action text. Never suppress missing information merely because its words appear in the answer.
- Preserve generic `[1]` unless its context establishes a citation.
- Honor explicitly requested metadata categories; a “Read technical details” option selects the complete variant.
- Keep separate proposals written-only; preserve proposal qualifications already in the main answer.
- Verify exact speech payloads and adversarial uncertainty cases with deterministic and browser tests; no additional inference call.
